6ece8953664f1897b245a9221309c973.title: Reconstruction
6ece8953664f1897b245a9221309c973.intro: A fundamental topic in algebraic vision is that of reconstructing a scene from images.

6ece8953664f1897b245a9221309d7ec.body: Of the ten possibilities, how many of the solutions can be real?
6ece8953664f1897b245a9221309d7ec.intro: The essential variety is a 5-dimensional variety of degree 10. A point correspondence gives a linear constraint so a five point correspondence should give 10 complex solutions.

6ece8953664f1897b245a9221309e430.body: How many linear constraints does a point correspondence in three views determine on the trifocal tensor variety ?
6ece8953664f1897b245a9221309e430.status: Numerical results suggest that there are 4 constraints but they only intersect the trifocal tensor variety in codimension three.

6ece8953664f1897b245a9221309e880.body: How do the 24 linear constraints lead a minimal problem? How many complex solutions are there?
6ece8953664f1897b245a9221309e880.intro: It is known that the trifocal tensor variety is dimension 18 with degree 297 inside of $\mathbb{P}^{28}$. It is also known that a six point correspondence in three views is a minimal problem.
6ece8953664f1897b245a9221309e880.status: Numerical methods show that each point correspondence only intersects the variety in codimension 3 and so will lead to a minimal problem. The degree is cut down at each step of imposing conditions leading to three complex solutions.

6ece8953664f1897b245a9221309fff4.body: In between the calibrated and uncalibrated cases there are partially calibrated cameras, say with both focal lengths known or with the center position known. What can we say about these situations?

6ece8953664f1897b245a922130a37a8.body: Given an algebraic curve in two views, when are they compatible? This is interesting when the cameras are fixed beforehand.

6ece8953664f1897b245a922130a5262.body: What is the Hurwitz form of the essential variety?

6ece8953664f1897b245a922130a5a5f.body: Can we use conic correspondence between two images to do reconstruction? Can we use point and curve correspondences to do reconstruction? Can we use cubic spline correspondences to do reconstruction?

6ece8953664f1897b245a922130a6ad5.body: Fix two cameras and two image curves. Is there is a curve in $\mathbb{P}^3$ that projects onto these two curves? What if we put restriction on degrees or smoothness?

6ece8953664f1897b245a922130ada30.status: Two approaches were suggested: That neither of the cameras are contained in the convex hull of the world points; or that $P r_i = \lambda x_i$ and $Q r_i = \mu y_i$ where $\lambda>0$ and $\mu>0$.
6ece8953664f1897b245a922130ada30.body: For a reconstruction what does it mean for all the points to be “in front” of the cameras? Can this easily be detected.

6ece8953664f1897b245a922130b3b52.body: The focal lengths of a pair of cameras can be written as a function of their fundamental matrix. During reconstruction fundamental matrices are constructed for which these focal lengths are complex. Is there an efficient way to detect if the this will occur before computing the fundamental matrix?

6ece8953664f1897b245a922130b5a71.body: How can we account for uncertainty, given the geometric structure of these problems? What if we replace points with disks?

9f1dec7ec10ffe36e3b0f46d0d018217.title: Geometry of F-singularities
9f1dec7ec10ffe36e3b0f46d0d018217.intro: Questions dealing with the properties of F-singularities

9f1dec7ec10ffe36e3b0f46d0d0190ac.name: Grauert-Riemenschneider for F-regular varieties
9f1dec7ec10ffe36e3b0f46d0d0190ac.body: Is there Grauert-Riemenschneider vanishing for $F$-regular varieties which admit a resolution?

9f1dec7ec10ffe36e3b0f46d0d01aaff.body: Does globally $F$-regular imply rationally chain connected?
9f1dec7ec10ffe36e3b0f46d0d01aaff.name: Global $F$-regularity and rational chain connectedness
9f1dec7ec10ffe36e3b0f46d0d01aaff.status: It's known that if $F$ is of globally $F$-regular type (i.e. $X$ is defined over a field of characteristic $0$, and $X_p$ is globally $F$-regular for $p \gg 0$), and $\mathbb Q$-Gorenstein, then $F$ is rationally connected.

9f1dec7ec10ffe36e3b0f46d0d01d381.name: Global $F$-regularity and Fano type
9f1dec7ec10ffe36e3b0f46d0d01d381.body: If $X$ is of globally $F$-regular type, does it follow that it is log Fano (in the sense that there exists a boundary divisor $\Delta$ with $(X,\Delta)$ klt and $-(K_X+\Delta)$ ample)? Even weaker, does it follow that $-K_X$ is big?
9f1dec7ec10ffe36e3b0f46d0d01d381.status: This is known if $\dim X = 2$, or if $X$ is a Mori dream space.  If $X$ is in fact globally $F$-regular, then it is log Fano for all $p$.  It's also true that if $X$ is of globally $F$-regular type, then $-K_{X_p}$ is big for $p \gg 0$.

9f1dec7ec10ffe36e3b0f46d0d01e269.name: Construction of $F$-pure centers
9f1dec7ec10ffe36e3b0f46d0d01e269.body: Suppose that $(X,\Delta)$ is a strongly $F$-regular pair.  Can we find a boundary $D \geq 0$ such that $(X,\Delta+D)$ is $F$-pure, with $p \nmid \text{index}(K_X+\Delta+D)$?

9230151c0d75ea6e6fdd392a6a120a84.body:
Call a braid $\beta$ parity if HHH$(\beta)$ is parity. Find necessary and/or sufficient conditions for a braid to be parity.

Are there operations on braids (for example, adding a positive number of full twists) which transform it into a parity braid or which preserve parity braids?

9230151c0d75ea6e6fdd392a6a121164.body: Are algebraic braids parity? If so find a (recursive) formula for HHH of an algebraic braid.

9230151c0d75ea6e6fdd392a6a12186c.body: There is a commutative family of braids built as products of FT$_k$, the full twist on the first $k$ strands, for $k \leq n$. Are the positive products in this family parity? If so, find a (recursive) formula for HHH.

9230151c0d75ea6e6fdd392a6a121f3c.body: In the presence of parity, there are two combinatorial formulas for HHH: one for localization of Hilbert schemes from the GNR conjecture and one from the Elias-Hogencamp-Mellit papers. How are these formulas related? How are they related to Demazure crystals?
